findings.detail: `selectedCols.includes(c)` runs once per cell of the full grid, inside the per-row/per-cell forEach. On the shape this feature actually targets — the fixture sheet is 43 columns wide, and the translator is routinely pointed at multi-thousand-row catalogue exports — a 40,000-row × 43-column sheet is ~1.7M `includes` scans on the main thread, executed synchronously at export time right after a long AI run. It is tens of milliseconds, not a freeze, so there is no user-visible impact today; I am flagging it because the fix is one line and the loop sits on the only code path every translation now takes. This would rise to medium if `selectedCols` ever became large or the grid loop gained more per-cell work.
findings.summary: overwrittenCells does a linear scan of selectedCols for every cell in the grid

findings.detail: `translate-real.xlsx` is documented as the product owner's own `Translate (2).xlsx` 'copied unchanged' — a 43-column Rewaa Simple import layout with 20 real Arabic product names and their prices. This is not a security-baseline violation: there are no credentials, tokens, or service-account material in it, so nothing here is exploitable. It is worth one conscious decision rather than a default, because the fixture is binary (it will not show up in future diff review) and because reproducing the exact customer-reported bytes is precisely what made the e2e test valuable — a synthesised fixture may not have reproduced it. Raising it only so the call is deliberate: if this repository is public or may become public, real catalogue data and pricing is business-sensitive even without PII. No action needed if the repo is private and the product owner supplied the file for this purpose.
findings.summary: Real internal reproduction file committed unchanged as a test fixture
